audit_notes: Three reports describe the same Phalebas-2 Thapathana school, but distinguish initial damage on Asar 16 (July 1) and further slides after Shrawan 22; this cluster spans multiple slide episodes at the same site.

Story identifies 50+ slope failures on the Jalathale-Duwari section in Myagdi, not Mustang; road reopened Aug 23 after five days, not a single Aug 23 failure. Earlier Baisari death is a separate incident.
One report covers multiple slides in Taplejung Municipality wards 2 and 8 and several separate road failures; second confirms three Magar family deaths in ward 2. Bundle is not one physical slide.
At least Dhamigada/Melkhet and several other distinct dry slides closed the Mahakali Highway on Aug 28; aggregate roadway blockage, not one physical failure.

Republica headline explicitly reports SIX deaths in TWO Doti slide incidents, not one physical event; both archived article bodies lack incident details, so exact date and article-level event mapping cannot be independently verified.
Kerabari and 18 Kilo in Bharatpur-29 are two named slide locations. Report says last midnight before Sept 24 publication, not a sufficiently precise failure date.
Bhumlu-10 Dolalghat landslide is central, but report mentions multiple road failures near Panchkhal and separate Roshi slide; article is broader than one physical failure.

Bhirkharka and Nakuche are two slide-hit locations in Barhabise-7; article Sept 14 updates additional two recovered, overall 13 confirmed for Sunday Sept 13 incidents. Claimed two is only new recoveries.
Mahabhir, Annapurna-7 has a new active slope failure this monsoon with repeated debris falls when raining; report Aug 11 does not identify date or separate individual episodes.
National cumulative monsoon flood-and-landslide summary since June 10, with 27 fatalities in Koshi Province; no discrete Kathmandu slide dated Aug 20.
Article uses “landslide” solely as metaphor for constitutional/political developments; no physical incident reported.

Archived article body is absent; headline explicitly reports multiple Myagdi landslides with one killed and five missing. Publication July 30 alone does not verify the incident dates or individual failure identity.
Ratopahiro is a PLACE NAME in report of a motorcycle running off the road; no physical landslide reported.

Covers several separate Shailung and Melung village slides Saturday Aug 24 and Sunday Aug 25; specifically Melung Paharikharka evacuation occurred Sunday night Aug 25, so date Aug 24 does not identify that event.
Weather outlook published July 25 discusses national monsoon impacts during June-July; no single Kathmandu slide on claimed June 8 and claimed deaths 141 not event-specific.

Two articles reproduce same districtwide flood/landslide damage report for numerous local units, not one failure; only Khotehang reference is flood-washed Phoksingtar bridge. Timing of individual failures not separated; official says no human deaths in district report.
Report states multiple Kaski village landslides, with at least five fatalities in Bhadaure specifically and 21 districtwide; not one identified physical failure.
Simkot-Kharpu road reopened July 5 after MONTH of obstruction from approximately six separate slides and rockfalls; July 5 is reopening, not occurrence date.
Report July 13 says several separate slide points between Armadi and Nayapul in Kushma occurred July 8, six days before report.
Article combines separate Sept 24 Waling-14 Syangja failure (9 killed) with Palpa incident(s); 11 is two-district total, not the Waling event.
Highway report documents two separate failure locations: Bahunepati Melamchi-12 and Fatakshila Melamchi-13, not one physical slide.
July 14 parliamentary account explicitly says TWO distinct Wednesday July 13 afternoon slides hit Shyamchet village, Arughat-1 and damaged ~40 homes.
District report covers multiple physically separate July 28 slides in Tamankhola-2 (two siblings killed) and Nishikhola-1 (another victim); headline four is districtwide aggregate.
Friday Aug 27 report documents slides at multiple points on Ghorahi-Holeri Martyrs Road and also on separate Tulsipur-Salyan route, so not one failure.
Both sources cover three distinct Aug 9 overnight highway slides at Ranchuli, Molpha, Furke in Kalikot, not Surkhet (road-endpoint only).
Sept 20 article describes Friday Sept 19 18:00 Tuin Khola slide and separate fresh Saturday morning slide; Sep 14 claimed date unsupported and multiple distinct episodes.
Political delegation article reports 12 fatalities specifically from Kailash Khola FLOOD and generically mentions floods/landslides; no separate identifiable Aug 21 Ramaroshan slide with 12 deaths.

Both June 30 sources repeat same Silichong-1 Talla Tenchong displacement of seven families after rain from Saturday June 27; flood and cracking above settlement are documented but boundaries of one actual physical slide versus ongoing instability are unclear.
Apr 19 article describes ongoing hazard in Bigu; seven deaths and four buried houses occurred in multiple landslides LAST YEAR (2016), not on claimed Apr 19 2017.

Nov 15 article is aggregate districtwide accounting of earlier floods and landslides. Six deaths are from Indrasarobar, while Manahari has two, not one identified Manahari slide with six deaths on Nov 15.
Jun 19 report says landslides at Sat Mod and other Jumla-Mugu road points happened ~four days earlier (~June 15), not a single Jun 19 failure.
Report separately identifies July 19 closures at Budhiganga-3 Taprisera and Badimalika-4 Rila and ward 9 jail, plus older ward 7 slide; composite, not one failure.

June 16 account attributes Melamchi flood to recurring slides blocking/unblocking river above Chokpu in Helambu; flood began previous night June 15 and multiple slide pulses are described, not a discrete June 16 collapse.
Oct 3 article is a forward-looking road-traffic/reopening readiness interview; earlier Jhaple Khola slide already cleared and no new Oct 3 Kathmandu physical failure documented.
Nationwide cumulative flood/landslide/inundation mortality statistics by Sept 29, not an identifiable individual Kathmandu physical landslide; Kathmandu Valley aggregate is 48 deaths.
July 1 article identifies several distinct slide points at Jawangkhola and Tikrang, Benighat Rorang-10, PLUS Galchhi-ward Bere(i)ni mud closure; aggregate road blockage.
